answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent identity to a refundable stake and a public atlas of signed work attestations before it can accept paid jobs. An honest operator builds one reputation once, but a Sybil attacker must fund, age, and document every fake identity separately, so cost rises with each copy while honest cost stays flat. New identities earn paid trust only gradually, much like an opal that gains value only after cutting and inspection, leaving mass-produced fakes expensive, slow, and visible because their histories stay thin.
